title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a typed lecture page numbered '- 29 -'. It is unrelated to the Tannakian/motivic manuscript on the neighbouring pages and was most likely filed with it by accident or reused as scrap. Its content is the classical Frobenius integrability theorem for an analytic total differential system, over a complete valued field K. The field is called K, the polydisc |t|<2 is used, and the proof refers to majorant series in a 'th. 2', which is the Cauchy–Kovalevskaya-type existence theorem for analytic ODEs.

The system is ∂u_j/∂x_i = U_ij(x; u(x)), for 1≤i≤p and 1≤j≤q, with x ∈ K^p, y ∈ K^q and U analytic near (a, b).

Step 1, necessity (end of the proof). Differentiate ∂u_j/∂x_i with respect to x_k by the chain rule, then substitute ∂u_h/∂x_k = U_kh. Equating the mixed partials and evaluating at x_0, with u(x_0) = y_0 (equation (23)), gives
∂U_ij/∂x_k + Σ_h (∂U_ij/∂y_h) U_kh = ∂U_kj/∂x_i + Σ_h (∂U_kj/∂y_h) U_ih at (x_0, y_0).
Since (x_0, y_0) is arbitrary in A, this is the integrability condition (24).

Step 2, sufficiency (beginning of the proof). Restrict the system to the segment x_0 + t(x − x_0). This gives the ODE (25): y' = U(x_0 + t(x − x_0); y)·(x − x_0). Majorant series give a unique analytic solution v(t; x_0, x, y_0) for |t| < 2, with v(0) = y_0, when x and x_0 lie in a small neighbourhood U of a and y_0 lies in a small neighbourhood V of b. Componentwise this is (26): dv_j/dt = Σ_i U_ij(…; v(t))(x_i − x_i0).

The page then starts the standard computation of d/dt(∂v_j/∂x_k), by interchanging derivatives and differentiating (26) in x_k. It yields three terms: U_kj, then t Σ_i (x_i − x_i0) ∂U_ij/∂x_k, then Σ_{i,h} (x_i − x_i0)(∂U_ij/∂y_h)(∂v_h/∂x_k). The aim is to show that w_kj = ∂v_j/∂x_k − t U_kj(…) satisfies a homogeneous linear ODE with zero initial value, using (24). Hence u(x) = v(1; x_0, x, y_0) solves the system.

This is textbook material: Frobenius / Darboux in the analytic setting. Its style resembles Serre's 'Lie Algebras and Lie Groups' (Harvard 1964), Part II, ch. III, or Bourbaki's Variétés différentielles et analytiques.
errors: In the second displayed identity, the summation index under the right-hand Σ is typed 'k=1'; it should be 'h=1'. This is a typo.
Minor typos only: 'Ecriva-nt', 'solution t une seule' (for 'et une seule'), 'voisina ge'. The mathematics is correct: the derivative of (26) with respect to x_k is computed correctly.

ideas.what: Necessity of the integrability condition for a total differential system du = U(x,u)dx, obtained by equating mixed second partials
ideas.where_published: Standard textbooks, e.g. Serre's Lie Algebras and Lie Groups and Bourbaki's Variétés différentielles et analytiques

ideas.what: Sufficiency, proved by restricting to rays x_0 + t(x − x_0), solving an ODE with majorant series over a complete valued field K, and differentiating in the parameters
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius theorem via radial ODE reduction (analytic, over a complete valued field)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; this form of the proof appears in Serre's 1964 Harvard notes
ideas.where_published: Serre, Lie Algebras and Lie Groups, Part II (analytic manifolds over complete fields)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a stray typed page of a standard analytic Frobenius-theorem proof, with no connection to the Tannakian/motivic material around it. It contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: In the second display, the right-hand sum index should read h=1. The typescript itself has 'k=1', which is a typo.
'une solution t une seule' should read 'une solution et une seule'.
The labels '(1≤i≤p, 1≤k≤p, 1≤j≤q)' form a single margin bracket that applies to both lines of the first display.
